new_statements.quote: (2) 轻声 轻声是普通话除四声外的一个特殊声调。白语是没有比较明显的轻声字的，所以学习普通话时必须仔细注意观察，凡是读轻声的音节，念时声音一定要短而轻。
new_statements.translation: (2) Neutral tone. The neutral tone is a special tone of Putonghua in addition to the four tones. Bai does not have fairly distinct neutral-tone syllables, so when learning Putonghua one must observe carefully: every syllable read in the neutral tone must be pronounced short and light.
new_statements.citation: Zhao Yansun 赵衍荪. 1981. 白语和汉语普通话的对比研究 [A contrastive study of Bai and Putonghua]. In 《民族语文》编辑部 (ed.), 民族语文论集, 47-110. Beijing: 中国社会科学出版社.

new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened: (page image, printed p. 94 = PDF page 98 of), scanned, lines 1589-1594 for the passage; lines 1-25 for p. 47), and a fresh 80-dpi render of PDF page 51 (printed p. 47). The quoted passage is on the p. 94 image verbatim, under the heading "（2）轻 声": 轻声是普通话除四声外的一个特殊声调。白语是没有比较明显的轻声字的，所以学习普通话时必须仔细注意观察，凡是读轻声的音节，念时声音一定要短而轻。 It continues 白族需注意以下这些常用的轻声字（轻声音节上不标调号）: followed by a list of Putonghua neutral-tone words, i.e. the section is pedagogical (teaching Putonghua to Bai speakers). The p. 47 image confirms author 赵衍荪, title 白语和汉语普通话的对比研究, and the three-dialect statement: 白语可分为剑川（…剑川县金华镇…）、大理（…喜洲五台镇…）、碧江（以怒江傈僳族自治州碧江县四区的白语为代表）三个方言, with Jianchuan as base and Dali/Bijiang forms in brackets;…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bai is a tone language in which every syllable bears one of its full tones; unlike Putonghua it has no clearly distinct neutral-tone (light, unstressed) syllables, i.e. no regular positional reduction of syllables. No positional word-stress rule is given.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about 轻声 (Putonghua neutral tone = phonetically short, light, unstressed syllables), made in a pedagogical contrast with Putonghua; it concerns Bai as a whole (the paper names Jianchuan, Dali and Bijiang = Northern as the three dialects, p. 47) with Jianchuan as the example base. It is not a word-stress (重音) rule; every syllable is described as carrying one of eight full tones.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is about Bai as a whole. Zhao Yansun's paper names three dialects, Jianchuan (Central Bai, cent2004), Dali (Southern Bai, sout2730) and 碧江 Bijiang (Northern Bai, nort2724), and uses Jianchuan as its example base with Dali and Bijiang forms bracketed; the author co-wrote Baiyu jianzhi (1984), which documents the Bijiang dialect. No opened source makes a stress statement specific to the Bijiang/Lama/Lemei varieties; Allen 2007's Luobenzhuo (Lushui) chart is the only Northern-specific phonology opened and it lists seven tones with no stress note.

sources.note: Sec. 一 lists the three dialects Jianchuan, Dali and Bijiang (碧江 = Northern) and takes Jianchuan as the base; 8 tones with tense/lax vowels, every syllable toned. Sec. 三 (2) 轻声, p. 94: Bai has no fairly distinct neutral-tone (light, unstressed) syllables, unlike Putonghua. No word-stress (重音) rule given.
